key_insight: CIC-Trap4Phish provides a unified, multi-format dataset of malicious and benign email attachments—including quishing (QR-code-based) artifacts—enabling end-to-end detection research across diverse attachment types that were previously fragmented across datasets.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a single, labeled resource covering multiple attachment formats (PDF, Office docs, images, archives, QR-containing media) and quishing examples, which hinder development and evaluation of generalized attachment-level phishing detectors.
method: Collect and curate real-world malicious and benign email attachments across multiple formats, with expert labeling for phishing/quishing intent.
Standardize extraction and representation: static parsing, metadata capture, embedded-URL extraction, OCR/QR decoding, and feature normalization across formats.
Publish dataset plus reproducible baselines and evaluation protocols to measure within-format and cross-format generalization of detectors.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a single, well-documented benchmark to train and evaluate attachment-level phishing/quishing models, improving robustness to diverse file types and embedded attack vectors and accelerating defensive research and deployment.
visual_elements: Pie/bar chart showing dataset composition by file format (PDF, DOCX, images, archives, QR-containing files).
Pipeline diagram: ingest → extraction (metadata/OCR/QR/URL) → labeling → model evaluation.
Annotated sample attachment image showing highlighted embedded malicious URL and decoded QR payload.
Benchmark chart comparing baseline model performance across formats and cross-format transfer results.
paper_title: CIC-Trap4Phish: A Unified Multi-Format Dataset for Phishing and Quishing Attachment Detection
paper_authors: Fatemeh Nejati, Mahdi Rabbani, Mansur Mirani, Gunjan Piya, Igor Opushnyev
